newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge says progress in Jewish bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge says progress in Jewish bomb probe.

text.p: The probe into the bloody 1994 attack against an Argentine Jewish community centre has gathered pace, the investigating judge said on Friday.

Judge Juan Jose Galeano said that investigators were now concentrating on tracking the movements, in the days prior to the attack, of a van that was packed with explosives and used as a car bomb to destroy the Jewish centre in Buenos Aires.

"Several lines of investigation have been built up on the basis of the trail of the vehicle used in the attack," said Galeano, quoted by the state-owned Telam news agency in the province of Tucuman, where he was attending a seminar.
Galeano said that "the investigation is not on the verge of dying out even though the newspapers and news broadcasts don't report on it every day."
An appeals court in September upheld the indictment of four Buenos Aires province police officers on charges they were "necessary accomplices" in the attack.
Authorities suspect the officers handed over the van to the attackers or to an intermediary.

The July 1994 attack killed 86 people and injured hundreds more. Argentina's police and courts have been criticised by Israel, the United States and Jewish leaders for failing to clear up the bombing, as well as a 1992 bomb attack on the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires, which killed 29 people.
